newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin to meet ministers to fix policies Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Jospin to meet ministers to fix policies Thursday.

text.p: France's Socialist Prime Minster Lionel Jospin will meet his cabinet ministers on Thursday to define government policies and prepare a speech to parliament likely on June 19, his office said on Monday.

Jospin would meet ministers from 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) on Thursday "to fix priorities for the government's action and get down to preparing the prime minister's policy declaration," Jospin's chief aide Olivier Schrameck said.

Jospin's general policy declaration to the newly-elected National Assembly was likely to be made in the afternoon of June 19. He had asked his 26-strong cabinet to outline priorities in "succinct" notes, Schrameck told reporters.
The Socialist-led government, including Communists and a Green environment minister, swept to power in an election on June 1 that ousted the centre-right allies of President Jacques Chirac.

Thursday's meeting between Jospin and his ministers will follow a formal cabinet meeting on Wednesday hosted by Chirac. Schrameck said the Wednesday meeting would fix the limits of each minister's responsibilities.

Jospin has said that fighting France's record 12.8 percent unemployment will be his top priority. The Socialists have promised to create 700,000 youth jobs and cut the work week to 35 hours from 39 with no loss of pay.
The new government has also attached conditions to accepting a single currency, the euro, from 1999.

France threw the European Union into turmoil on Monday by telling its partners it wanted time to study an already agreed deal designed to keep budget deficits from ballooning after the euro is introduced.
New French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told his counterparts in Luxembourg that Paris wanted to consider -- but not renegotiate -- the agreed plan.

Separately, France's Minister for Employment and Social Security Martine Aubry reiterated on Monday that Jospin would keep campaign pledges and that the new policy would be the result of a "true work of collective reflection" by the cabinet.
She urged measures ranging from help to revive the construction sector to measures to help sort out the fate of illegal immigrants.
